solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Dressed warmly to be picked up and transported (4)

indicatorNotes.to be picked up: what is picked up is caught by the ear, so the word is heard rather than seen

blocks.note: dressed warmly = wrapped up; keep the sound and respell it

annotation.surface: Someone bundled up in warm clothes is lifted and carried off somewhere.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Picked up and transported' reads as one action on the bundled person; it splits, with 'transported' meaning enraptured, not carried.
annotation.definitionFit: To be transported is to be carried away with delight, which is exactly what rapt means.

entries.clue: Make fresh evaluation with reference to Jenny? (8)

blocks.note: re = with reference to, as in a memo heading
a jenny is a female donkey: jokily an ASS-ESS, formed like lioness or tigress

annotation.surface: Someone looks again at something to do with a person called Jenny.
annotation.walkthrough: Jenny looks like a woman's name, but a jenny is a she-donkey; the setter invents 'assess' as a feminine of ass, like lioness from lion, and the question mark owns up to the liberty.
annotation.definitionFit: To reassess is to evaluate something again, making a fresh evaluation.

entries.clue: Solicitor supporting therapist? (8)

blocks.note: pro = in favour of, supporting
a therapist is one who cures, a curer; the question mark flags the loose fit

annotation.surface: A lawyer backs up a therapist, perhaps in a professional dispute.
annotation.walkthrough: Solicitor looks like the British name for a lawyer, but here it means one who solicits, as a pimp does, which is the old sense of procurer.
annotation.definitionFit: A procurer obtains prostitutes for clients, soliciting on their behalf.

entries.clue: A teaser CID actively roots out (10)

indicatorNotes.actively: the letters are set in motion, moving into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A puzzle that the detectives of the CID energetically hunt down.
annotation.walkthrough: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of a British police force; here its letters are just fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: To eradicate is to root out, destroy completely.

entries.clue: Broadcast sound part of withdrawn tabloid article (5)

indicatorNotes.part of: the answer is a part of the words that follow
indicatorNotes.withdrawn: drawn back, so the letters are read in the backward direction

blocks.note: five letters straddle the join, from the O of tabloid to the R of article, and are read upwards

annotation.surface: A newspaper story that has been pulled is talked about on the airwaves.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue the letters run upward, so 'withdrawn' works naturally; the definition is two words, since radio is sound broadcasting.
annotation.definitionFit: Radio is broadcasting in sound alone, as opposed to television.

entries.clue: Infernal place to soften paint (9)

blocks.note: Dis is the classical underworld, Hades
to temper = to soften or moderate

annotation.surface: Somewhere hellish where paint is left to go soft.
annotation.walkthrough: Dis, the Roman god of the underworld and his realm, is a crossword regular; distemper is a cheap water-based wall paint.
annotation.definitionFit: Distemper is a kind of paint made with glue or size, used on walls.

entries.clue: Cell 15 rocked — brilliant group (13)

indicatorNotes.rocked: shaken about, so the letters are disturbed into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 4 letters
15 is the answer to 15 down, anagram fodder, 9 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A prison cell is shaken up by a dazzling band of performers.
annotation.walkthrough: The 15 means you need 15 down's answer before this one opens; 'brilliant' is literal, since a constellation is a group of shining stars.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the stars of Orion or the Plough shine brightly and are seen as one pattern, so 'brilliant' is meant literally.

entries.clue: Tear into one’s own supporter (6)

indicatorNotes.into: one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: on your tod means on your own: Tod Sloan, rhyming slang for alone
a tear is a rip; it goes into T-OD

annotation.surface: Someone rounds angrily on the person who backs them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On your tod' is British slang for on your own, from rhyming slang Tod Sloan, a jockey. 'Tear into' reads as attack, but splits into the rip and its container.
annotation.definitionFit: A tripod is a three-legged stand that supports a camera or similar.

entries.clue: Sailor pinching uniform given base gesture (6)

indicatorNotes.pinching: taking hold of something between, so the letter goes inside
indicatorNotes.given: a piece is given, added on at the end

blocks.note: an old salt is a sailor
U = uniform in the NATO alphabet; SAL(U)T
e is the base of natural logarithms

annotation.surface: A sailor steals a uniform and is then shown a rude sign.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Base gesture' looks like one phrase for something vulgar; 'base' breaks away as the mathematical e, and the gesture is a respectful one.
annotation.definitionFit: A salute is a formal gesture of respect, such as a raised hand.

entries.clue: Woke peer denied skirting American journalist (7)

indicatorNotes.denied skirting: the word is refused its skirting, the letters round its edges, so only the inside is kept

blocks.note: a peer is a BARON; without its outer letters B and N it leaves ARO
US = American
ED = editor, the crossword's standard journalist

annotation.surface: A politically aware lord is stopped from dodging a reporter from the States.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Skirting' reads as avoiding the journalist, but it is a noun: the skirting of BARON, its edges, is what the peer is denied. 'Woke' is the past tense of wake, not the political word.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the past tense: a sleeper who woke was stirred from sleep, the old sense of the verb before its sexual one.

entries.clue: Unsteady girl tips things in absence of special illumination (5,8)

indicatorNotes.Unsteady: the letters wobble out of their order
indicatorNotes.in absence of: the named letter is missing from the fodder

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 14 letters before one comes out
S = special; one S is removed, leaving 13 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A wobbly girl knocks things over in a room without proper lighting.
annotation.walkthrough: Fourteen letters of fodder for thirteen in the answer is the sign that something has to go: one of the S's, standing for special.
annotation.definitionFit: Strip lighting, long fluorescent tubes, is a form of illumination.

entries.clue: Star, evidently easy-going, that may give one the time of day (7)

annotation.definition: that may give one the time of day

indicatorNotes.evidently: easy-going is laid-back, and evidently the LAID is to be written back

blocks.note: the sun is a star
easy-going = laid-back: LAID, back

annotation.surface: A relaxed celebrity is friendly enough to pass the time of day with you.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Give one the time of day' means be friendly to someone; the definition takes it literally, since a sundial tells the time only by day.
annotation.definitionFit: A sundial shows the time from the sun's shadow, so it gives the time only in daylight.

entries.clue: Original position of Romanesque grotesque lacking marks (6,3)

indicatorNotes.grotesque: distorted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.lacking: the named letter is absent from the fodder

blocks.note: anagram fodder before the deletion
M = marks, the old German currency; ROMANESQUE without M leaves ROANESQUE
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: An art historian's note on where a grotesque carving first stood, before it wore smooth.
annotation.walkthrough: Romanesque and grotesque are both architecture words, and the surface keeps you in a cathedral; back to square one means back to the start.
annotation.definitionFit: Square one is the starting point, the original position, as on a board game.

entries.clue: Swimmer in River Test? That’s not unknown (5)

indicatorNotes.That’s not: the result is what the word is when it is not the named letter, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: a test is a tryout
y is an algebraic unknown, and it is the letter the tryout loses

annotation.surface: An angler asks what swims in the River Test, a famous English trout stream.
annotation.walkthrough: The Test, in Hampshire, is one of England's best-known trout rivers, so the answer really is in the picture; the capital T hides that Test is also the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A trout is a fish, a swimmer found in rivers.

entries.clue: Dizzy Gillespie curtailed plans to release a stunner? (8,4)

indicatorNotes.Dizzy: spinning, so the letters are jumbled
indicatorNotes.curtailed: its tail is cut off, losing the last letter
indicatorNotes.to release: the named letter is let go from the word

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters
PLANS curtailed is PLAN; releasing the A leaves PLN
the A released from PLAN
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Jazz trumpeter Dizzy Gillespie cuts short his plans to put out a sensational record.
annotation.walkthrough: Dizzy Gillespie is so fixed a name that 'Dizzy' passes for part of it; it is the anagram signal, and a stunner here is something that knocks you out.
annotation.definitionFit: A playful sense, flagged by the question mark: a stunner is usually a beauty, but here it is anything that knocks you out cold.

entries.clue: Symbolic stuff in religious texts adopted by states (9)

indicatorNotes.adopted by: taken in by, so the first piece goes inside the second

blocks.note: states = nations
OT = Old Testament, taken inside the states after their first letter

annotation.surface: Symbols in scripture that various countries have taken up.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface runs definition and wordplay together as one scene; 'in' is only the join between them.
annotation.definitionFit: Notations are systems of symbols, as in musical or mathematical notation.

entries.clue: Ecstasy tablet elevating family member? Or... (8)

indicatorNotes.elevating: raising it up, so in a down entry the word reads bottom to top

blocks.note: E = ecstasy, the drug
a tablet is a PILL, turned upward to LLIP
sis = sister

annotation.surface: A pill of ecstasy is getting a sister high, or something worse, left unsaid.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue trails off into its own definition: the three dots after 'Or' are an ellipsis, and the question mark admits it.
annotation.definitionFit: An ellipsis is the mark ... showing that words have been left out.

entries.clue: Distinction rising setter’s awarded in Florence after run (8)

indicatorNotes.rising: going up, so in a down entry the word reads upward
indicatorNotes.’s awarded: the setter has been awarded the next piece, which is added on
indicatorNotes.after run: only the part of the word that comes after R, for run, is taken

blocks.note: the setter is ME, rising to EM
the word itself
the letters of FLORENCE after the R, R being run

annotation.surface: An up-and-coming setter wins a prize in Florence after a stint of running.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rising' reverses the setter's ME. The cricket abbreviation R = run tells you where in Florence to start reading.
annotation.definitionFit: Eminence is distinction or high standing, as in a scientist of great eminence.

entries.clue: Fruit, sort of cross, precisely delivered (8,4)

indicatorNotes.delivered: a speech is delivered out loud, so the word is to be heard

blocks.note: the Victoria Cross is Britain's highest award for gallantry
plumb = exactly, as in plumb in the middle; said, it is plum

annotation.surface: Someone angrily and exactly hands over a piece of fruit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry, but it is the medal; a Victoria plum is a common British variety of red plum.
annotation.definitionFit: The Victoria plum is a sweet red variety of plum, a fruit.

entries.clue: A case of thieves from Bow going to pot? (3,3)

annotation.definition: A case of thieves from Bow going to pot?

blocks.clueFragment: A case of thieves from Bow
blocks.note: reads as a gang of East End crooks; in Cockney rhyming slang a tea leaf is a thief, so it is a case (bag) of tea leaves
reads as going to ruin; literally, heading into the teapot

annotation.surface: A gang of East End crooks is going to the bad.
annotation.walkthrough: Bow is in London's East End, home of Cockney; in rhyming slang a tea leaf is a thief, so a case of thieves is a bag of tea leaves, and it is going into the pot.
annotation.definitionFit: A tea bag is a small bag of tea leaves put into the teapot.

entries.clue: Dread Henry catching queen being bedded by two lots of men (6)

indicatorNotes.catching: Henry takes hold of what follows, attached to it
indicatorNotes.being bedded by: the queen lies between two others, as in a bed

blocks.note: H = henry, the unit of inductance
OR = other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
R = Regina, queen
the second lot of men, closing round the R

annotation.surface: Henry VIII seduces a queen who is then passed around by soldiers, a truly dreadful story.
annotation.walkthrough: OR for other ranks is a standing convention for men; two lots of it make the bed, OR-R-OR.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both nouns name overwhelming fear, as in 'filled with horror'.

entries.clue: What about returning officer’s age? (5)

indicatorNotes.about: going around, so one piece encloses the other
indicatorNotes.returning: coming back, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: eh? = what?
an officer is a COP, returning to POC, which goes inside the EH

annotation.surface: Someone asks how old the official running an election is.
annotation.walkthrough: A returning officer is the official who runs a British election and declares the result, and that two-word phrase must be split up.
annotation.definitionFit: An epoch is an age, a distinct period of history.

entries.clue: Facility withdrawn by inspector (initially to improve working customs) (9)

indicatorNotes.withdrawn: drawn back, so the word is read backwards
indicatorNotes.by: the next piece is placed by it, beside it
indicatorNotes.initially: only the first letters of the next words are taken

blocks.note: facility = skill, ART, withdrawn to TRA
DI = detective inspector
first letters of to and improve
on = working, as a machine is

annotation.surface: An inspector shuts down a facility, meant as a first step towards better working practices.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Facility' reads as a building, but it is ease or skill, ART. The bracket looks like an aside and holds half the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Tradition means inherited customs; the singular stands in for the plural sense here.
annotation.definitionNote: customs is plural, tradition singular in form but collective in sense

entries.clue: Exhausted Aston Villa losing heart in play. Pounding from The Hammers here? (5)

indicatorNotes.Exhausted: emptied out, leaving only the outer letters
indicatorNotes.losing: the named letters are taken away
indicatorNotes.heart in: the heart of the next word, its middle letters

blocks.note: ASTON emptied of its inside leaves AN
the word itself, before the loss
the middle of P-LA-Y; VILLA losing LA leaves VIL

annotation.surface: A tired Aston Villa side lose their nerve against West Ham, known as The Hammers, and take a pounding.
annotation.walkthrough: Aston Villa and West Ham (nicknamed The Hammers) are English football clubs, so the surface is a match report; the definition takes the hammers literally, beating metal on an anvil.
annotation.definitionFit: An anvil is the iron block on which a smith's hammers pound metal.

entries.clue: You are overwhelmed by most of UK national dish (7)

indicatorNotes.overwhelmed by: swamped by the other piece, so it ends up inside
indicatorNotes.most of: all but the last letter is used

blocks.note: a Briton is a UK national; most of it is BRITO
UR = you are, in text-speak, placed after the first letter of BRITO

annotation.surface: Someone is swamped by the British national dish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'National dish' looks like one phrase, pointing at fish and chips or roast beef; 'national' belongs with UK, and the dish is Mexican.
annotation.definitionFit: A burrito is a Mexican dish of filling rolled in a tortilla.

entries.clue: Foremost of VIPs fronting New Orleans function sent back meat (7)

indicatorNotes.Foremost of: only the first letter of the word is taken
indicatorNotes.fronting: going in front of what follows
indicatorNotes.sent back: sent backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: the first letter of VIPs
NO = New Orleans, the city's abbreviation
sine is a trigonometric function; NO+SINE sent back is ENISON

annotation.surface: Top guests at a New Orleans party send their meat back to the kitchen.
annotation.walkthrough: Function reads as a party, but it is the mathematical sine.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the flesh of deer is a game meat, served roasted or in stews.

entries.clue: Domestic market in recycled beers launched by petrol station (6,4)

indicatorNotes.recycled: put through again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.launched by: set going by the other piece, which comes first

blocks.note: a garage sells petrol
ales are beers, rearranged to SALE

annotation.surface: A petrol station starts selling recycled beer to home buyers.
annotation.walkthrough: Domestic here means held at home, from a householder's garage, not national as in the domestic market.
annotation.definitionFit: A garage sale is a sale of household goods held at a private home, a domestic market.

entries.clue: Man possibly controlled by Doris Lessing? (4)

indicatorNotes.controlled by: held inside the words that follow

blocks.note: dorIS LEssing

annotation.surface: A question whether a male character is under the novelist Doris Lessing's control.
annotation.walkthrough: Man looks like a person; it is the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland, and 'possibly' marks it as one example of an isle.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Man, in the Irish Sea, is one island among many, and 'possibly' signals the example.
